scenes.headline: take()
scenes.subtitle: Grabbing the first N rows efficiently.
scenes.narration: The take action returns the first N rows of a DataFrame to the driver, without scanning everything.

scenes.headline: What take does
items: Returns the first N rows as a Python list
Reads only enough partitions to satisfy N
Cheaper than collect for a quick peek
Returns Row objects, unlike show which prints
scenes.narration: Take returns the first N rows as a Python list, reading only enough partitions to satisfy the request. That makes it cheaper than collect for a quick peek, and unlike show it returns Row objects rather than printing.

scenes.headline: Peeking with take
scenes.narration: We call take with three to grab the first three rows into a list, then loop over them and print each as a dictionary. Because take stops as soon as it has enough rows, it avoids scanning the entire dataset.

scenes.text: Use take for a lightweight sample and collect only when you truly need every row.
scenes.narration: Reach for take when you just need a lightweight sample, and reserve collect for the rare cases where you truly need every row.
